rules.reason: Workloads must reach image registries, package mirrors and AWS APIs, so egress from a security group is open by default. A stricter allow-list or VPC endpoints is a per-customer decision the generated files do not make.

Workloads must reach registries, package mirrors and Azure APIs, so outbound rules are open by default. A stricter allow-list or private endpoints is a per-customer decision the generated files do not make.
The public service is open to the range the person chooses (everyone by default) and the generator warns when it is open to the whole internet; the other services are not.
The load balancer serves plain HTTP only when no ACM certificate is given, and the generator warns about it. With a certificate, HTTP redirects to HTTPS.
The load balancer is the public entry of a web service by design; who can reach it is set by allowed_cidr, and the tasks behind it accept traffic only from it.
Buckets are encrypted with AES256 (S3-managed keys). Customer-managed keys need a KMS key and key policy per project, which is the customer's choice and not made by the generated files.

Key Vaults are protected by RBAC but have no network ACL block, so they answer from any network. A default-deny ACL needs private endpoints, and the in-app release writes secrets from outside the network, so it is not set yet.
A storage account's network rules default to allow. Setting default deny needs the customer's own address range or a private endpoint, which the files do not know yet.
An AKS API server is reachable from any address. Authorized ranges need the address of the person running kubectl, which the files do not know; to be offered as a setting.
ECR tags are mutable so a release can reuse a tag such as latest. Immutable tags need a unique tag for every release, which the release flow does not enforce yet.
The generated Deployments do not set a read-only root filesystem. It needs a writable temp volume per stack, to be added.
The generated Deployments rely on the container's own settings instead of a pod-level security context. To be added with the read-only root filesystem.
A CloudFront distribution has no web application firewall in front unless the design includes one. The generator should add one when the design is public.
Storage accounts let trusted Microsoft services bypass the network rules, which Azure's own services need for logs and backups; to be reviewed per design.
AKS clusters are created without a network policy. To be offered as a setting with a default.
